entries.lead: TPC-DS maintenance refuses to run against enforced primary keys
entries.text: TPC-DS data maintenance now follows TPC-DS 4.0.0 clauses 5.2.3, 5.2.5, 5.2.7 and 5.3: refresh data sets come from `dsdgen -update`, are generated before any timer starts and are loaded into staging tables inside each function's timed interval through the platform's generic loader, and the 11 spec functions (LF_CR, LF_CS, LF_I, LF_SR, LF_SS, LF_WR, LF_WS, DF_CS, DF_SS, DF_WS, DF_I) run as set-based SQL.
details: The synthetic Python row generator and the per-row UPDATE handlers are removed; a run seed is passed to `dsdgen` as `-RNGSEED` only when one is set; the spec defines no UPDATE functions. Maintenance runs on platforms that declare refresh support (DuckDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Snowflake); other platforms report the phase as skipped.

Each result records `run.maintenance_method` (`dsdgen_refresh_sets`) and, per function, the refresh set, the staged row counts and the rows inserted or deleted per table. Maintenance timings from earlier BenchBox versions used the `synthetic_rows` method and are not comparable: `benchbox compare` and the analytics and platform comparison APIs refuse to compare results recorded with different maintenance methods.

The kit's refresh keys start at 1 in every refresh set and overlap the base keys (`getUpdateBase` indexes the wrong table), so maintenance refuses to run when primary keys are enforced on a maintenance target table (DuckDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite) and names the tables and the `--tuning notuning` way out; Snowflake does not enforce primary keys and runs. Returns deletes match in-range sales by order or ticket number plus item.
Loading refresh data never truncates a warehouse table and stops the function on any rejected or missing row.
